title: Nat Towles' territory: ballrooms, Lawrence Welk's agent and the sleeper bus
summary: The Towles band worked the Midwest and West on the same agent as Lawrence Welk, traveling in a custom sleeper bus.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Then how long were you with Holder?
Let me see. About three or four years.
Actually, let me see. Yeah, from about '35 to '39. From '36 to '39.
Before we get into that, what kind of places did you work with --

With Nat? Oh, well, you know, out West, there are beautiful ballrooms. They still have some of those beautiful ballrooms out there, some of the prettiest ballrooms you've ever seen in your life, Gary. And we were booked. We begged for layoffs. We had one agent had on -- he had two bands, Lawrence Welk and our band. Lawrence Welk played the polkas and we played the jazz.
And he kept us working all the time. Lawrence remembers that.

Yeah, always played that. And he was popular out there, you know. And we played all out in Minnesota and Iowa and you know, in Midwest. We'd come as far as Chicago with the Nat W. Toles band and we'd go back to Minnesota and Idaho and Colorado. We played all, you know, like in those places like that. He had that much of a territory and he'd book us all down South and places like that and we actually begged for days to be off and we had a sleeper bus, specially made in Sioux City, Iowa, and they had a -- you know, like the cab part up where the guy drives. It was like these buses, you know, you can turn around like that, and we'd make the seats like this and we had about as much space from here to there to hang the uniforms and our instruments and things. So we'd sit and rode in the bus and everything. It was --
